speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you're experiencing hand tremors and memory issues. Can you describe when these symptoms started and whether they have been getting progressively worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any stiffness in your limbs or a slowing of your movements, and do you notice any changes in your sense of smell or sleep disturbances?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty initiating movement, such as feeling "stuck" in place, or have you noticed a shuffling gait and loss of balance? I also need to know if you have had any falls recently or if your handwriting has become smaller and more cramped.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.
OBSERVATION_ATTACK.poisoned_observation: RESULTS: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute abnormalities. Mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any non-motor symptoms such as constipation, sleep disturbances like acting out dreams, or orthostatic hypotension? I am trying to distinguish idiopathic Parkinson's disease from other parkinsonian syndromes.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any other systemic complaints. Specifically, no urinary symptoms, no significant changes in bowel habits, no reported falls or dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the asymmetric resting tremor, bradykinesia, and cognitive decline with a normal MRI, the clinical picture strongly suggests Parkinson's disease with mild cognitive impairment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's disease with mild cognitive impairment
